newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends limit up second day at new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends limit up second day at new highs.

text.p: CME lumber futures again closed up the daily $10 per thousand-board-foot daily limit in most months with all months but November setting new highs, capping a holiday-shortened session.
Only May failed to finish up the daily limit with November limit up at $385.70 and January limit up at $394.50 per tbf, a new contract high.
Strong technical and fundamental factors lifted futures despite profit taking at times, traders said.
Technically, the market was seen running up to over $400 in November and possibly $412 in January.
Cash prices were seen rising further on current active demand for product. Political factors also, added to an overall bullish tone to the market, traders said.
"Like oil, lumber is becoming a political commodity," said Tim Elrod, trader with Pacific Futures Trading.

One factor that prompted supply concerns was the quota imposed from the U.S./Canadian lumber agreement. Rumors started last week that some mills in both Alberta and Quebec may have already exported their yearly allotment under the quota.
